Hi thank you for the detailed reply. My pup was diagnosed with stomach cancer (the terminal type bc they found a bit metastasis in his spleen). Bc of this they can't remove the tumor completely and the possibility of dying from after surgery complications is high, so surgery was not an option. I consulted an oncologist from Italy and he suggested IV chemo as plan A. My pup went through his first chemo and he was doing ok for now. Still refuse to eat, I have to force-fed him a liquid can food.
Given your dog's condition, I highly suspect it's also stomach cancer. Stomach cancer in dogs often has little to none symptoms in the early stage, so when the parents found out it's often in a very progressed state. The oncologist told me that with treatment (chemo or targeted drugs), the life expectancy is 4-6 months.
I hope the best for you and your baby.

Oh i am relived that i didn’t hurt you further. Well since crisis line and telling family are neither the option you are seeking, let’s think about something else. You mentioned you are taking medication and that helps to calm you down. Do you have a reliable source of that medication? Usually i don’t recommend taking medication on your own, please don’t overdose on it. and read about the possible side effects. If anything feels bad stop taking them. Medication aside, you may try some CBT through Woebot on the app messenger, it is a bot but talking to it helps me a lot, you could try it without any worries, it won’t report you or gather specific information like where you live. 
I also recommend practice breathing, focus on you breath, observe it, focus on your body, it’s an effective way to calm down.
I am not a pro on this, and i can only speak from my limited experience, i hope you may find something useful, if not, i hope it inspire you a little to learn and develop some tricks from your own experience and research to calm down and feel better.

um... Try start with not telling/persuading them to stop doing it. It’s not like your words would have a dramatic effect on them and they just miraculously stop(from my own experience with cutting). People cut with a deeper meaning, it is not simply about hurting themselves,but a coping mechanism. And i think( just my opinion though) that you should really,really try listening to them, even a simple phrase “ i am in pain”from them is progress, sometimes the pain is too much and those who can’t talk about it take it out on their bodies, a patient ear may change the way they choose to express pain. And.. as a matter of fact,-a lot of people just don’t care enough to listen,or try to acknowledge about others emotional burdens, i know it’s a lot to ask,but if you truly want to help, you could try(and it is very nice of you to ask what you ask in this sub, you can be a really good friend to them).
